citations.assessment: The referred entry explains the rejected identification by parsing Rava as the son of Rabbah bar Rav Huna in Chullin. It distinguishes that story from the parallel with Rav Huna in Beitzah.
Abaye addresses Rav Avya to appease Rav Yosef. The actual sequence gives weakness, absence, and the discussion of praying musaf before eating.

The Bavli has Avya sit on the bed before Rava. Heilprin uses a different seating construction, so the translation and source contrast are kept explicit. Rav Nachman’s blessing falls on 46b:1 in this edition.
The elder asks Rav Huna about slaughter on a festival. The dismissal and subsequent dialogue with Huna’s son Rabbah are distinct from the Chullin story.
The question is addressed to Rabbah bar Rav Huna. The raven remark and response by his son Rava explicitly describe the elder as from Pumbedita.
The named pairing concerns uncertainty about produce. This witness reads Rabbah bar Rav Chanan, whereas the root uses the abbreviation rendered Rabbah bar bar Chana.

Both visitors enter to Rabbah bar bar Chana, who is already eating and hides the fat. The base reads elder Avira. Rabbenu Chananel reads Rav Avya and a different companion name. Preserve the alternatives.
Avya reports Rav Yosef about how to roll the grain. Abaye gives a different procedure in the same teacher’s name.
Rav Avya reports Rabbi Ammi on removing the fat and describes the observed practice.
Avya without elder married Rami bar Pappa’s sister. Rav Yosef lists two errors, and Abaye and Rava add distinct objections.
Avya without elder marries Rami bar Chama’s sister. The loss of the ketubah and the Rav Yosef and Abaye exchange continue on 57a.
Rav Pappa’s public exposition involving the elder Avya concerns how festivals count toward mourning. The causative formula is retained without deciding a wider relationship.
The full passage says Avya’s hand came out of joint while he was seated before Rav Yosef, as confirmed by the repeated Mishnah wording and the ensuing remedies discussion.
Avya’s objection starts at the end of 22a. Its second-tithe weighing example and the reply continue on 22b.
Avya and Nechemyah cite distinct verses for the commanded Hanukkah blessing.

The sword-as-ornament exchange explicitly presents alternate questioners and addressees involving Abaye, Rav Dimi, Rav Avya and Rav Yosef. Preserve the compressed report with the multiple alternatives noted.
This daf has a separate Rav Avya statement in a sequence of remedies. The named Abaye/Yosef conversational alternatives appear at 63a.
The hinge socket answer is attributed here to Rav Adda. Eruvin gives Rav Avya in the related doorway discussion.
The lexical entry gives Avya and explicitly records Adda in other copies. Its explanation is the socket into which the hinge fits.
The current text reads Rav Acha son of Rav Avya and concerns placement of tefillin. This supports the proposed reading in this occurrence without altering Heilprin’s Hebrew.
The previously uncited objection is located in the basket-of-figs example. A later line also refers to Rav Huna bar Avya in a dream, a different designation.
